title: The same invoice shows the same due date to users in other locations
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure you are also enrolled at location B, which is in another time zone.
  • Make sure Invoice A, dated Oct 5, 2026, at the test location, belongs to a customer who holds one of the shop's own terms, due on day 10 of the following month.
  • Make sure a second user, user B, without Settings → Finance, works in location B.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open invoice A.
  2. Switch location to location B.
  3. Open invoice A again.
  4. In user B's browser, open invoice A.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The due date reads Nov 10, 2026.

Step 2:

  • You now work in location B.

Step 3:

  • The due date still reads Nov 10, 2026.

Step 4:

  • User B also sees Nov 10, 2026 (the term list loads for every user).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R6a: “The same invoice shows the same due date to every user, whichever location they are working in. A vendor invoice created by receiving a delivery uses the delivery's location, even when the receiving user is working in another location.”
  • S7-R6: “Due dates are counted on the calendar of the location the invoice or vendor invoice belongs to, never the location of the user, API connection or import that creates or views it, so a daylight saving change inside the span never moves the date: an Edmonton invoice dated Oct 5 on "10th of the following month" is due Nov 10 (not Nov 9).”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions: “The organization's credit term list itself (the terms that fill those dropdowns, and which one is the default) loads for every user in the shop, as today,”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
